title: Good practices for advancing climate and nature-related risk management
date_evidence: 8 May 2026 — Blog post by Frank Elderson, Member of the ECB's Executive Board and Vice-Chair of the Supervisory Board
key_claim: Around two-thirds of supervised banks do not yet systematically link climate and nature materiality assessments to risk management actions.
frame_summary: Elderson argues supervisory good practices now extend from climate into nature, and that sound management of these risks is ordinary prudential work banks must complete.
verbatim_quote: around two-thirds of them do not yet systematically link these to risk management actions
verbatim_list: Nature-related risks are an area where approaches are more in their infancy.
notes: Primary supervisory-advance anchor; publication exactly at the soft window edge (92 days).

title: Good practices for climate and nature risk management - Observations from the ECB's five-year climate and nature risk programme (2020-25)
date_evidence: May 2026 — Good practices for climate and nature risk management – Observations from the ECB's five-year climate and nature risk programme (2020-25)
key_claim: Most of the newly added good practices in the ECB's 2026 compendium concern nature risks, drawn from more than 60 supervised institutions.
frame_summary: The compendium frames nature-risk management as an observed, spreading bank practice rather than a future aspiration, grounding supervisory expectations in what peers already do.
verbatim_quote: Most of the newly added good practices concern nature risks.
verbatim_list: The newly added good practices – whether complementing existing ones or newly added – are drawn from more than 60 different institutions, representing more than half of the institutions directly supervised by the ECB.
notes: Same publisher as the blog but a distinct primary document; the compendium is the substantive artefact. Year tokens 2020-25 are the programme-period in the document title, confirmed current May 2026 edition.

publisher: Network for Greening the Financial System
title: NGFS provides new tools to manage nature-related financial risks (2026 Nature Package)
key_claim: The NGFS 2026 Nature Package gives central banks and supervisors practical tools (data, modelling, supervisory practice) to integrate nature-related risks into their work.
frame_summary: The NGFS argues nature loss is a source of financial risk that central banks and supervisors should now be equipped to assess, normalising nature within the prudential toolkit.
verbatim_quote: It is increasingly important for central banks and supervisors to understand the risks linked to nature loss.
notes: Structural anchor: canonical multilateral framing for the prudential channel, 3-6 month band.

title: Commission updates product scope and tools to support EUDR implementation
key_claim: The July 2026 Delegated and Implementing Acts complete the EUDR simplification package while keeping the December 2026 application date.
frame_summary: The Commission presents the changes as simplification that preserves the regulation's deforestation-free due-diligence architecture and its application calendar.
verbatim_quote: The measures adopted today complete the simplification package presented by the Commission in May 2026, which also included an updated Guidance document and Frequently Asked Questions.
verbatim_list: It removes cattle hides, skins and leather, re-treaded tyres, soybeans for sowing, articles of vulcanised rubber, conveyor and transmission belts, and aircraft and motor vehicle seats from the scope of the Regulation. At the same time, it adds soluble coffee, certain palm oil derivatives and frozen cattle tongues.
notes: Border-compliance track; freshest Tier 1 in the base.

title: Rapport durabilite 2025 - L'action durable de la Banque de France et de l'ACPR
key_claim: The Banque de France now publishes nature performance indicators, including the share of its portfolios exposed to sectors highly dependent on nature.
frame_summary: The Banque de France positions nature exposure as a measurable balance-sheet property a central bank reports on itself, extending the precedent it set with its biodiversity footprint.
verbatim_quote: en publiant la part de ses portefeuilles exposée à des secteurs fortement dépendants de la nature
notes: Multi-language Tier 1 (French). Own-balance-sheet demonstration of the prudential channel. '2025' is the reporting year in the title; the report itself was published 26 June 2026 (confirmed on page).

title: EU Deforestation Regulation: Commission publishes simplification package ahead of December 2026 application date
date_evidence: 15 May 2026 (publication date on Hogan Lovells website)
key_claim: The simplification package cuts compliance cost sharply while leaving the EUDR's due-diligence architecture and application date unchanged.
frame_summary: Counsel reads the package as cost relief within an unchanged and binding regime, advising clients to keep preparing for December 2026.
verbatim_quote: these measures are expected to reduce annual compliance costs for companies subject to EUDR obligations by about 75% compared to the original EUDR
verbatim_list: the fundamental architecture of the EUDR remains unchanged
notes: Carries the 75% cost-reduction figure and the architecture-unchanged assessment.

title: European Union: EU Commission Publishes Simplification Review of EUDR
date_evidence: 08 May 2026 | European Union: EU Commission Publishes Simplification Review of EUDR
key_claim: The Commission concluded the EUDR will not be reopened and existing implementation timelines continue to apply.
frame_summary: Counsel emphasises regulatory certainty: simplification is not repeal, and the compliance clock is running.
verbatim_quote: the EUDR will not be reopened and that the existing timelines for its implementation continue to apply
notes: Second legal read corroborating the no-reopening conclusion.
